    route_of = {}  # node -> route_id
    rcap = {}  # route_id -> load

        routes[rid] = [c]
        route_of[c] = rid
        rcap[rid] = demands[c]
        rid += 1

    # Precompute depot distances for customers
    dep_d = {}
    for i in depot_nodes:
        dep_d[i] = d(depot, i)

    # Compute savings list deterministically
    savings = []

        di = dep_d[i]
        for j in depot_nodes:
            if j <= i:
                continue
            # typical directed savings; we allow both directions by using i<j pair but decide merge endpoints.
            s = di + dep_d[j] - d(i, j)
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    # Sort by savings desc, then i asc, then j asc
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

    # For deterministic endpoint handling, we only merge in the orientation that connects tail(i) -> head(j)
    def can_merge(ri, rj, i, j):
        if ri == rj:
            return False
        if rcap[ri] + rcap[rj] > cap:
            return False
        r1 = routes[ri]
        r2 = routes[rj]
        # i must be tail of r1
        if r1[-1] != i:
            return False
        # j must be head of r2
        if r2[0] != j:
            return False
        return True

        rj = route_of[j]

            del routes[rj]
            del rcap[rj]

            rj2 = route_of[i]

                rcap[ri2] += rcap[rj2]
